executive_summary: The autonomous AI agent ecosystem in 2026 has shifted toward deterministic, stateful graph architectures. LangGraph leads enterprise workflows requiring cyclic state and human-in-the-loop controls. CrewAI excels in intuitive role-playing agent orchestration and rapid prototyping. Microsoft AutoGen maintains a strong presence in conversational multi-agent research.

assumptions: Focus on actively maintained open-source agent frameworks in 2024-2026
constraints: Every statement backed by official documentation or verified benchmarks

key_findings.title: State Graphs as the Production Standard
key_findings.summary: Enterprises favor graph-based state machines (LangGraph) over opaque autonomous loops due to determinism, auditability, and replayability.

key_findings.title: Role-Playing Multi-Agent Simplicity
key_findings.summary: CrewAI captures high developer velocity for collaborative workflows through clear persona abstractions.

key_findings.title: Conversational Coordination
key_findings.summary: AutoGen offers flexible event-driven multi-agent conversations, particularly in research and simulations.

entities.name: LangGraph
entities.description: Library for building stateful multi-actor applications with LLMs using explicit graph computation.

entities.name: CrewAI
entities.description: Framework for orchestrating autonomous agents with specific personas, goals, and tools.
tradeoffs: Less deterministic than explicit state graphs

entities.name: Microsoft AutoGen
entities.description: Multi-agent conversation framework enabling multi-agent chat and modular communication.
tradeoffs: Dynamic conversation flows can be harder to audit

comparison.analysis: LangGraph enforces typed state channels; AutoGen relies on chat message history; CrewAI maintains task buffers.
